title: A Second Method of Making
summary: A simpler method Pathak ji uses himself: divide the length from the mouth-hole to the low Pa into six equal parts, then split the lowest four sixths into two, three, four and five parts to place twelve notes, komal Dha up to Pa. For tubes seven or eight times the circumference, use sevenths instead.

blocks.text: One more method of making the bānsurī, simpler than the one above, is given here. I myself make [bānsurīs] by it. Its rules are set out in the following 7 ślokas

blocks.verse:
द्वितीयोऽपि प्रकारः स्याद् बंशी निंर्माण कर्मणि।
निर्माणे येन सौविध्यं सर्वथा स्यात्सुरैषिणाम्।47।
blocks.text: There is a second method too in the work of making the bānsurī, by which those who seek tunefulness may find every convenience in the making.

blocks.verse:
बंशादौ मुखरः प्रोक्तः बंशान्ते पंचमः स्थितः।
मध्यान्ते तु विनिर्णीताः क्रमात् सर्वे स्वरा इह।48।
blocks.text: At the start of the bamboo the mouth-hole is set, at the end of the bamboo stands Pa; and from the middle to the end all the notes are here fixed in order.

That is, for the convenience of makers a second method is also being given. Here the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) is at the start of the bamboo, Pañcama (P̣a) at the end, and all the remaining notes are placed from the middle to the end. See Figure No. 16.

blocks.verse:
मुखरन्ध्रमितं वशम् षड्भागे परिकल्पयेत्।
अधस्तात् प्रथमों भागस्तस्मिन् भागद्वयं मतम्।49।
blocks.text: Divide the bamboo, measured up to the mouth-hole, into six parts; the first part from below is held to have two parts.
Divide the length from P̣a to the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) into six equal parts, and divide the first part from the bottom into two parts.

blocks.verse:
मन्द्रपात् प्रथमस्यान्ते स्थाप्यताम् ऋजु धैवतः।
तत ऊर्ध्व द्वितीयान्ते शुद्ध धैवत इष्यते।50।
blocks.text: From the mandra Pa, at the end of the first [half] let ṛju (komal) Dhaivata be placed; above that, at the end of the second, śuddha Dhaivata is wanted.
At the end of the first part from the bottom place komal Dhaivata, and at the end of the second, śuddha Dhaivata.

blocks.verse:
षष्ठांशात् षष्ठमम् भागम् न्यूनंकृत्वा तु धैवतः।
अखण्डिते तु षष्ठांशे धैवतः षष्ठमे मतः।51।
blocks.text: Dhaivata [is placed] after taking a sixth part away from the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth); but when the sixth is left undivided, Dhaivata is held to be at the [full] sixth.

If mandra Pañcama is open in the bānsurī, then for the distance of Dhaivata, that is the first hole, above it: divide the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth) again into six parts, take one part away from it, and mark Dhaivata at whatever distance remains. Then, when making the hole, make it a small hole and enlarge it while testing the note. If Pañcama is not open but is made by a hole, the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa will remain whole.

But if the distance of the open Pañcama from the mouth-hole is nine 'miti', Dhaivata will be at the distance of the full ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth). Take miti to mean paridhimāna (measure of the inner circumference).

blocks.verse:
षष्ठांशे द्वितीये तु भागें भागत्रयम् मतम्।।
निषादौ द्वौ तथा षड्जः स्थाप्यन्ताम् क्रम पूर्वकम्।52।
blocks.text: The second sixth is held to have three parts; there let the two Niṣādas and Ṣaḍja be placed in order.
Divide the second ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth) into three parts and place, in order, the 3 notes komal Ni, Ni, Sa at equal distances.

blocks.verse:
षष्ठांशे तृतीये तु भागें भाग चतुष्पृयम्।
रिषभौ द्वौ च गान्धारौ तत्र स्थाप्याः क्रमेण वै।53।
blocks.text: The third sixth [has] four parts; there the two Ṛṣabhas and the two Gāndhāras are to be placed in order.
In the same way, divide the third ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth) into four parts and place komal Re, Re, komal Ga, Ga.

blocks.verse:
षष्ठांशे चतुर्थेतु भागाः पंच प्रकल्पिताः।
तत्रादौ त्रिसु भागेषु मध्यमौ पंचमः स्मृताः।54।
blocks.text: The fourth sixth is divided into five parts; in the first three of these parts are the two Madhyamas and Pa.

And divide the fourth ṣaṣṭhāṃśa (one-sixth) into five parts and place Ma, Ma′ and Pa in the first, second and third parts, in order. Beyond this, by leaving out the [remaining] part, the place of Pa falls of itself at 2/5, as before. For these divisions you can take the help of paper; folding it will make the dividing easy. This method will suit only a length of nine times. If the length is near eight or seven times, then instead of the ṣaṣṭhāṃśa take the saptāṃśa (one-seventh): mark off four saptāṃśas from the bottom, and in those same four saptāṃśas make two, three, four and five divisions in order, and place the 12 notes.
